newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean escapes to S.Korea through mined border.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean escapes to S.Korea through mined border.

text.p: A North Korean man daringly escaped to the South on Sunday morning through one of the world's most heavily fortified borders, the National Defence Ministry said.

A ministry statement said the 38-year-old civilian, dressed in a military-style top, black pants and mustard-coloured sneakers, was seen and led to safety by a South Korean soldier on duty at the eastern end of the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ).
The statement identified the defector as Jang Young-kwan, but said the name was a pseudonym.

Many North Korean escapees in the South use false names to protect themselves from terrorist attacks and to protect their families in the North. Families of North Korean defectors are often sent to gulags or sometimes executed.
South Korea has been more cautious about identifying defectors since Li Il-nam, a nephew of North Korean leader Kim Jong-il's former wife, was shot in a Seoul suburb in February and later died.
The attack occurred three days after Hwang Jang-yop, one of North Korea's top ideologues, sought asylum at the Seoul consulate in Beijing.
Defections through the heavily mined, four-km (2.5 mile) wide DMZ are less common. In February, a barefoot North Korean woman fled across the minefields and razor wire barriers to the South.
More North Koreans are defecting as their country slides into famine. The South Korean government is building a camp south of Seoul to house up to 500 North Korean escapees.
